headline: Elon Musk denies SpaceX AI device report, calls WSJ claims 'utterly false'
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported SpaceX demoed a handheld AI device, slimmer than an iPhone, to investors. However, Elon Musk quickly responded on X, stating the report is 'utterly false'.
details: The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX demoed a handheld AI device to investors ahead of its initial public offering. The purported gadget was described as slimmer than an iPhone and powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon chip.

It reportedly runs on a proprietary operating system and integrates with xAI services, including the Grok AI assistant. The device was said to offer a way to access xAI's models without needing a traditional smartphone.
However, Elon Musk swiftly denied the report on X, stating it is 'utterly false.' This came just minutes after the initial story was published.

The rationale for such a device could be to bypass app store revenue cuts and platform rules imposed by companies like Apple and Google. This strategy aligns with other tech giants like Meta, who are also developing their own hardware platforms.

While Musk has previously expressed skepticism about making mobile devices, SpaceX's partnership with T-Mobile in July 2025 to offer Starlink satellite access on smartphones made a similar AI device plausible. The company already has a foundation for integrated connectivity.

Despite the initial report's details, any new product associated with Musk's companies often requires a degree of skepticism. The device may have been primarily intended to excite investors rather than signal a definitive new product direction.

headline_marked: Piggy AI plugin [[writes 80–94% less code]] for developers, cutting token costs by up to 77%
headline: Piggy AI plugin writes 80–94% less code for developers, cutting token costs by up to 77%
summary: This new AI coding agent plugin forces simpler, more efficient solutions, drastically reducing code lines and API costs. It makes AI think like a senior developer.
details: AI coding agents often over-engineer solutions, generating verbose code that senior developers would avoid. Piggy is a new plugin designed to make AI agents think like experienced developers, prioritizing the simplest working solution.

Tests across five common tasks (email validation, debounce, CSV sum, countdown, rate limiter) on Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus models showed significant improvements. Piggy reduced lines of code by 80-94% and token costs by 47-77%.

The plugin enforces a "lazy mode" approach, prioritizing existing helpers, standard library functions, native platform features, and already-installed dependencies. It only generates new code as a last resort, aiming for single-line solutions where possible.

Piggy is compatible with popular AI coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Devin, Kiro, Gemini, and OpenCode. It offers various commands for lazy mode enforcement, code review, auditing, and complexity scoring.

The plugin aims to reduce bugs, lower API call costs, and speed up responses by minimizing code complexity. It offers modes from "lite" (suggesting alternatives) to "ultra" (extreme YAGNI enforcement).
